title: Design, Fabrication, and Characterization of Continuous Magnetic Fibre Polymer Composites
content: This study investigates magnetic polymer composites reinforced with continuous ferromagnetic fibres as an alternative to conventional particle-based soft magnetic composites for electromagnetic circuit applications. Epoxy specimens reinforced with continuous steel wires or an equivalent amount of ferromagnetic powder were fabricated and compared with non-magnetic reference materials and additively manufactured polymer–carbon fibre composites. Their mechanical and magnetic properties were characterised through tensile testing and measurements of dynamic magnetic permeability and magnetic losses using ring-shaped specimens. These measurements enabled the assessment of magnetic behaviour and energy dissipation under alternating excitation. Finite element simulations were also performed to evaluate the influence of reinforcement morphology and predict the behaviour of composites with increased magnetic fibre volume fractions. Continuous magnetic fibre reinforcement substantially improved both ultimate tensile strength and effective magnetic permeability compared with particle-reinforced composites containing an equivalent ferromagnetic content. Numerical modelling indicated that increasing the fibre volume fraction to 30% may provide magnetic performance comparable to conventional core materials under operating conditions below magnetic saturation. The developed composites show potential for use as structurally integrated magnetic circuits in 3D-printed, low-volume electromechanical devices, including customised vibration energy harvesters.
